response.text:
I can’t access your mailbox directly. I can, however, give exact steps you can run to remove all Uber messages and stop new ones from arriving. Which email provider (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, Apple Mail, etc.) are you using? If it’s Gmail, follow these steps:

Delete all existing Uber messages (Gmail web):
1. In Gmail’s search box paste:
   from:(@uber.com)
   and press Enter.
2. Click the top checkbox to select messages on the page.
3. Click “Select all conversations that match this search” (appears above the message list).
4. Click the Trash icon to delete them (or Archive if you prefer to keep them but out of your inbox).
5. Empty Trash later if you want them permanently removed (Trash > Empty Trash now).

Auto-delete future Uber messages (Gmail web):
1. Click the “Show search options” icon in the search box.
2. In the From field type: @uber.com
3. Click “Create filter”.
4. Check “Delete it” (and optionally “Also apply filter to matching conversations”).
5. Click “Create filter”.

Alternatives and cautions:
- You can open a recent Uber message and use the three‑dot menu to “Unsubscribe” (if present) or “Block” the sender, but blocking may miss other Uber domains.
- Consider archiving instead of deleting if you want to keep receipts or trip records.
- Check Trash and Spam folders after deletion in case something important was removed accidentally.

If you use another provider, tell me which and I’ll give the exact steps for that service (or provide the exact filter text to paste).
